extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and peer reviewers), journal editors, and platform operators in the life sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational standards for conducting journal-agnostic peer review of preprints via the Review Commons platform, and for how authors and affiliated journals should use the resulting 'Refereed Preprints'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review must be substantiated, critical, and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: One round of review requires typically three researchers spending each on average 6 h to provide a substantiated, critical, and constructive scientific analysis of a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is a scientific activity where interpretations can be challenged, evidence scrutinized and findings compared to preexisting knowledge. Reports should help authors improve the strength and clarity of their study; reviewers function to 'assist delivery' rather than to act as judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-agnostic reviews (focus on science, not journal fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: By disentangling the review process from the context of a specific journal, Review Commons encourages reviewers to focus on the science rather than journal-specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes more objective and portable reviews; reviewers should not conflate scientific evaluation with editorial judgements about scope or journal 'fit'.

rubrics_metrics.name: When requesting additional experiments, evaluate the work 'as is'
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting additional experiments, reviewers are asked to evaluate the work 'as is' and not as it would have to be in order to meet the editorial 'bar' of a given journal in the eyes of the referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extra experiments should be justified by the current manuscript's needs, not by an ambition to tailor the paper to a higher-impact journal. This reduces asking for work that is only required to meet journal-specific thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews may include assessment of significance and placement in context
rubrics_metrics.description: The review does not need to be restricted to technical aspects, but it can also include an expert assessment of the significance of the study for the field by placing it in the context of the existing literature and assessing the nature of the reported advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to judge both technical rigor and the study's contribution/advance relative to prior work; this aids authors and future journal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of scientific assessment from editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and editorial evaluations are two important but distinct tasks; their conflation can undermine efficiency and clarity. Review Commons separates scientific assessment (peer review) from journal editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting Refereed Preprints provides unfiltered access to in-depth analyses and avoids forcing a binary accept/reject dependency between review and publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial editorial triage by Managing Editor (scope and significance filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Commons Managing Editor carries out an initial editorial assessment in consultation with an academic advisory board to select manuscripts that fall within the scientific scope of the platform and that represent a significant advance: that is they are of concrete value for a specific scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because resources are finite, the platform triages submissions and selects those likely to benefit most from in-depth review; the Managing Editor corresponds directly with authors, while peer review is run by EMBO Press scientific editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select for 'significant advance' / concrete value to a community
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts selected should represent a significant advance — that is they are of concrete value for a specific scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit selection standard used at intake to prioritize limited reviewer resources; it implies assessing novelty, importance, and targeted community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Refereed Preprints publicly (transparency, avoid binary accept/reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, authors are invited to make the full set of reviews and their response publicly available as 'Refereed Preprints' on bioRxiv and to submit the manuscript and the referee reports with a response to one of the journals affiliated with Review Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting provides transparent, in-depth analyses by independent experts and means the outcome is not constrained to an all-or-none acceptance decision at a partner journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated journals will use Refereed Preprints for informed decisions (avoid fresh re-review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consortium of journals has agreed to use Review Commons Refereed Preprints for making informed decisions without starting the peer-review process from scratch; affiliate journals have agreed not to review the manuscripts afresh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may ask for additional advice only to arbitrate on issues raised by the referees or seek complementary expertise; they are encouraged not to request an editorial opinion on journal fit and not to re-contact original referees except when required for an informed editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review transfer and authentication by Review Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviews are transferred to bioRxiv and to target journals directly by Review Commons on behalf of the authors, thereby authenticating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures integrity of the review record and reduces burden on authors to compile and transmit reports; it also supports journal trust in the reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer name sharing requires explicit consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Names will be shared only with explicit referee consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors take the Refereed Preprint to other journals, those journals can approach Review Commons for the referee names and reports, but names are only disclosed with referees' permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors retain ownership and freedom to choose journals or withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: With Review Commons, authors take ownership of the reviewer reports and are free to decide what they deem best for their work: choose a Review Commons affiliate or any other journal and/or post the reports alongside their preprint; there is no tie in: authors can withdraw at any point to submit anywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' control over reports and choice of venue is preserved; partner journals will not know to which affiliate a manuscript has been submitted beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated journals should avoid editorial re-assessment of 'fit' before accepting reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliated journals are encouraged to only re-contact the original referees if this is required for an informed editorial process and not to request an editorial opinion on journal fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the portability of reviews and prevents reintroduction of journal-specific scope judgements into the scientific assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform is experimental and metrics-driven; policies will evolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons is an experiment; the current workflow and policies are initial conditions and will evolve — the platform will collect evidence and report data about reviewer adaptation, researcher uptake of publicly posting Refereed Preprints, and sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should expect policy and operational changes based on measured community responses; scalability and equilibration are design goals tied to community needs for dissemination speed, transparency, and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of limited reviewer resources and selective coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing in-depth reviews by highly competent experts for every single preprint on bioRxiv is unlikely to be achievable in the near future due to finite reviewers and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constraint motivates the initial editorial triage and selection for manuscripts of sufficient scope and impact; it is an explicit operational limitation shaping platform policy.
